text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **

The English inventor of the miners' safety lamp Sir HUMPHREY DAVEY was born in 1770. He also discovered nitrous oxide - "laughing gas". He ruined his own health because of his curiousity about the taste of chemicals.
The American who invented the electric motor, the electromagnet and the telegraph, JOSEPH HENRY, was born in 1797.
American novellist and journalist best-known for "God's Little Acre" and "Tobacco Road" ERSKINE CALDWELL, was born in 1903.
American chemist WILLARD FRANK LIBBY, who developed radio-carbon dating, was born in 1908.
Australian artist CLIFTON PUGH was born in 1924. He also wrote "Death of a Wombat" and "Dingo King".
English/Australian actor RON GRAHAM, who starred in the long-running TV series "Certain Women", was born in 1926.
British entertainer TOMMY STEELE, who began his career as a pop singer, was born in 1936. He became a star of stage and screen musicals such as "Half a Sixpence".
Australian media magnate KERRY PACKER, who changed the face of cricket with the introduction of the World Series competition, was born in 1937.
One of Australia's top entertainment promoters MICHAEL EDGELY was born in 1943.
US bass player and singer with 'Angel' MICKEY JONES was born in 1952. The band was formed out of the remains of several east coast groups in 1975.

British singer with 'Bananarama' SARAH DALLIN was born in 1961. The group's first record was in 1981. Hits included "Shy Boy" (1982), "Venus" (1986), "Love In The First Degree" (1987), "I Want You Back"(1988) and "Help" (1989).
**EVENTS**
1900 : A reward was announced for the first person to
communicate with extra-terrestrials. Communication with Martians didn't count as they were considered to be too easy to contact.
1903 : The WRIGHT brothers ORVILLE and WILBUR made

aviation history with the first powered flight. Before an audience of only five people the "Kitty Hawk" made four flights, the longest lasting about one minute. The aircraft travelled 276 metres at an altitude of several metres.
1929 : Peters ice-cream went on sale for the first time
in Melbourne.
1952 : US President-elect EISENHOWER and General

MACARTHUR met in New York to discuss ways of ending the Korean War. MACARTHUR was sacked by President TRUMAN as Supreme Commander of the Far East. EISENHOWER had recently returned from Korea and his meeting did not win him favour with TRUMAN.
1967 : Australia's Prime Minister HAROLD HOLT disappeared

and was presumed drowned at Portsea on the Victorian coast. Although 59-year-old HOLT was a strong swimmer conditions were very rough. Military and civilian divers and search teams continued looking for the Prime Minister for days. His body was never recovered. He was Minister for Labour from 1940 to 1941 and then again from 1949 to 1958 and federal treasurer from 1958 to 1966 when he succeeded Sir ROBERT GORDON MENZIES as prime minister. His brief prime ministership was dominated by the Vietnam War, to which he committed increased Australian troops.
1979 : A New Zealand man was given a Royal Pardon after

serving eight years of a life sentence for one of the country's most infamous murders. ARTHUR THOMAS was convicted of the 1970 murder of a couple on a neighbouring farm. HARVEY and JEANETTE CREW were murdered and their 18-month-old daughter was left alone in their blood-stained home. The pardon came after a year-long investigation into the evidence. After being freed THOMAS said he wanted to track down the killer and clear his name.
1987 : In Britain, DAVINA DURBIN became the world's first
triple heart, lungs and liver transplant patient.
1989 : In Romania, as many as two thousand
anti-government protesters were massacred in the city of Timisoara.
1994 : A Spanish Appeal Court ruled that fugitive

Australian businessman CHRISTOPHER SKASE should be freed, without condition. SKASE had spent most of the year under guard in hospital, as Australian authorities sought his extradition. Spanish judges later claimed they'd accepted his appeal, on the grounds that he was too ill to return to Australia by boat or plane. Since this decision his health has appeared to improve, with the oxygen mask and wheelchair being discarded.
